m.x: Quartic ease-in/out. Applies a quartic (fourth-power) curve that acceleratessharply from the start, then decelerates sharply into the end. The motionis symmetric: the first half mirrors the ease-in, and the second half mirrorsthe ease-out. This produces a more dramatic acceleration and deceleration thanquadratic or cubic easing, making it suitable for snappy, high-energy transitions.

p.x: The value to be eased, in the range [0, 1].

r.x: The eased value, in the range [0, 1].
